interfaces.title: Private human interface
interfaces.people: Owner/applicant, authorized work/Git collaborator/reviewer and specifically authorized operator using a supported browser/device context.
interfaces.direction: Actor to product: intended goal, supplied content and exact resource/revision context. Product to actor: only authorized views, validation and actual operation result.
interfaces.authority: Product sign-in is not a universal grant. Check exact actor/resource/action/current state, including direct references and administrative powers. Employer context is IF-02, not implicit access to the private workspace.
interfaces.meaning: Required/optional conceptual inputs follow the target operation and dictionary. Source/draft/live/actual material, task/item/Sprint, account/provider context and current versus stale evidence are distinguishable. English/German content is manual; time meaning follows relevant domain.
interfaces.lifecycle: No automatic source propagation, publication, sending, progress inference, acceptance, deployment or physical reclamation from navigation/save alone. Restrict diagnostic context; no secret/private-content examples.
interfaces.repetition: Re-evaluate changed authority/revision. Unknown consequential save/action uses exact-operation reconciliation before repeat; browser refresh/back/duplicate submission is not a universal idempotency promise.
interfaces.capacity: Supported workloads, input limits and responsiveness/accessibility measures need scoped 13/primary criteria; no fixed number is inferred from demo resources.
interfaces.compatibility: Browser/device/viewport, keyboard/focus/labels/contrast, representation and supported language matrix remain to be reviewed; no native mobile app, public API or universal browser compatibility is introduced.
interfaces.gates: Exact UI/client matrix, full action/state permissions and quantitative interaction criteria remain proposed. Accepted explicit apply/publication is not reopened.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable

interfaces.title: Protected employer representation
interfaces.people: Employer viewer without a product account; resume owner controls link/password separately in private context.
interfaces.direction: Viewer to product: exact link/password context and requested selected page/evidence/PDF/language. Product to viewer: permitted exact representation or bounded denied/unavailable result.
interfaces.authority: Current applicable link/password/optional adopted expiry and exact selected resource rules govern every entry path, including direct file/PDF references. No viewer account or private workspace authority is invented.
interfaces.meaning: Published presentation, effective PDF mode, generated/uploaded variant, uploaded language identity and actual artifact availability are separate. Neither mode does not disable page/link; missing language cannot silently become private/unrelated fallback.
interfaces.lifecycle: Confirmed link disablement prevents fresh protected access. Already downloaded bytes are outside recall. Actual submitted material is not whichever live view the employer later opens.
interfaces.repetition: Fresh password/link checks and existing/in-flight/cached contexts follow separately reviewed policy. Interrupted retrieval is not complete; safe repeated read does not grant access after revocation or imply content immutability.
interfaces.capacity: Representation size/processing/retrieval expectations need actual agreed limits/conditions; no download/session/expiry duration invented.
interfaces.compatibility: Exact presentation/encoding/content-serving/client details remain design/acceptance work; selected PDF categories are scope, not proof every variant exists.
interfaces.gates: Credential rotation is a source/state policy with proposed details, not an exhaustively modeled new operation contract. Session/cache/in-flight/language/rendition policy remains scoped.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable

interfaces.title: Authorized file/PDF exchange
interfaces.people: Authorized uploader/requester, intended content owner/resource and product processing/retrieval responsibility; employer retrieval also applies IF-02.
interfaces.direction: Into product: intended evidence/PDF/asset bytes plus owner/resource/language/provenance/replacement intent. Out: truthful admission/processing/availability and permitted exact retrieval result.
interfaces.authority: Upload, replacement, association, retrieval, cleanup and administration are separate powers. Actual effective policy/content/reference/current capacity conditions govern intended candidate; resource reference/filename is not permission.
interfaces.meaning: Byte candidate versus admitted versus usable content are distinguishable. File identity, actual submitted-set provenance, language/variant and association survive interpretation; client metadata is not proof of valid type or historical equivalence.
interfaces.lifecycle: A new candidate or failed replacement cannot silently destroy required prior/actual material. Source replacement does not rewrite actual sent history; cleanup and quota release need reference-aware eligibility and actual effect.
interfaces.repetition: Concurrent growth/replacement/changed policy require reviewed current capacity and reference semantics. Partial/unknown upload/processing is not usable success; no universal resumable-transfer/retry guarantee is chosen.
interfaces.capacity: Format/content validation, byte/aggregate units, current growth/temp/retained accounting and processing limits require reviewed values. Idle free disk is not a concurrent-admission proof.
interfaces.compatibility: Exact accepted representations/formats/encoding/metadata fields, transfer mechanism and safe-serving behavior remain design/criteria work; no arbitrary import/export or general file hosting is added.
interfaces.gates: No quotas, whitelist, content-handling technology, storage backend, cleanup schedule or universal cancellation behavior is selected.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable

interfaces.title: Gmail provider operations
interfaces.people: Connected user, selected intended Google account and Gmail provider, under conditional actual access.
interfaces.direction: Product to provider: explicitly authorized read/search/draft/send/reply intent for exact account/context. Provider to product: permitted content, identifiers and attributable acceptance/rejection/limit/access-loss/uncertain result.
interfaces.authority: Product session/grants and actual selected-account provider capabilities are different prerequisites. Reading, composing/persisting drafts, sending and replying are not one implicit permission.
interfaces.meaning: Provider/account/message/conversation/draft identity and current sender/recipient/body/attachment/reply context remain attributable. Final confirmation must match actual intended send content; acceptance is not recipient delivery/read.
interfaces.lifecycle: Disconnect stops new dependent provider action under reviewed rules; retained local copies and draft ownership need explicit policy. Do not expose credentials/private mailbox through general project membership, logs or examples.
interfaces.repetition: Changed reviewed content requires renewed confirmation. Unknown send requires same-attempt reconciliation before separately eligible resend; reconnect does not blindly replay pending sends. Draft create/update/retry semantics need their own exact contract.
interfaces.capacity: Actual provider access, limits/cost/applicability and supported operation constraints need evidence. No polling, timeout/backoff, volume or quota values are invented.
interfaces.compatibility: Exact mechanism/scopes/representation/version and access/verification conditions are not chosen or newly verified here. Provider compatibility requires later applicable findings; no support for arbitrary mail providers is added.
interfaces.gates: OAuth has not been created. User Gmail capability is not an authentication/recovery notification channel. Draft and connect/disconnect contracts are source-derived families, not falsely claimed among the 39 selected operations.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable

interfaces.title: Calendar provider and local mapping
interfaces.people: Activity owner, selected intended account/calendar and Google Calendar provider; local-only goals are compared explicitly.
interfaces.direction: Product/provider: only selected authorized event operations and relevant event/version/time result. User/product local branch: local activity or association-only unlink, without implied provider mutation.
interfaces.authority: Local operation authority differs from provider write capability. Exact account/calendar/mapping/action and field authority are established before dependent provider action; local unlink does not need active provider write access.
interfaces.meaning: Local/provider identity, optional mapping, selected authoritative fields, relevant local/provider versions, all-day/time-zone meaning and freshness/conflict state are distinguishable. Local notes and application associations are not provider-owned grants.
interfaces.lifecycle: Local unlink does not delete provider event; provider removal is a distinct observed external change. Disconnect/reconnect does not delete/recreate/replay local/provider state by default. Reminders need separate actually available delivery capability.
interfaces.repetition: Concurrent local/provider changes remain conflicts/stale until explicit reviewed resolution. Ambiguous provider mutation is reconciled against same intended object; reconnect alone does not make mapping Fresh.
interfaces.capacity: Actual provider limits, freshness/latency/workload and reminder-delivery conditions require defined evidence; no timing or automatic sync direction is invented.
interfaces.compatibility: Exact time representation, fields, event identity/mapping, mutation mechanism and compatibility/version policy remain scoped design/acceptance work; no bidirectional or last-write-wins default.
interfaces.gates: OAuth absent. Direction/time/conflict/deletion/reconnect policy remains proposed; local-only paths can still be specified without a configured provider.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable

interfaces.title: Real Git-client boundary
interfaces.people: Actually supported real Git client/user and intended product-hosted repository/ref. Browser PR/review/merge management is IF-01 context, not an invented Git wire operation.
interfaces.direction: Client to product: intended authorized clone/fetch/pull or push/ref-change context. Product to client: real repository content/history/ref or explicit rejection/conflict/incomplete/unknown result.
interfaces.authority: Repository read, ref write/protected-ref, review/merge and target deploy authority remain separate. Exact current intended repository/ref permission and expected/evaluated revision context apply to non-browser entry.
interfaces.meaning: Repository/ref/object/revision meaning is real Git domain content, not a browser simulation. Moving ref names are not immutable evaluated review/check identities. Client transfer outcome and actual ref state require attributable evidence.
interfaces.lifecycle: Rejected/stale/unknown ref changes do not imply an unchanged target or completed rollback. Required history/references and retention/recovery need repository-specific contracts, not a universal file purge.
interfaces.repetition: Interrupted read transfer is incomplete; unknown push needs actual intended ref reconciliation before consequential repetition. Changed source/target/reviews require re-evaluation for merge in IF-01.
interfaces.capacity: Object/transfer/history growth and real client compatibility/resource behavior need scoped conditions/evidence; no size, connection or client/version limit invented.
interfaces.compatibility: Neither SSH nor HTTPS transport nor Git engine is selected. Administrative root SSH previously used to inspect the demo host is not evidence of product Git-client authentication/interoperability; development GitHub is not product hosting proof.
interfaces.gates: Actual supported client/transport/credential/protection/recovery choices remain proposed or unverified. No new public developer API, webhook or universal Git-client compatibility.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable

interfaces.title: Conditional execution and separate deployment target
interfaces.people: Authorized trigger/actor, defined workflow/code context, conceptual execution boundary and separately approved intended deployment target.
interfaces.direction: Into execution: supported exact definition/revision, scoped authority/resources/secrets and permitted trigger. Back: attributable actual attempt/output/state. Separate target exchange: independently authorized artifact/revision effect and target outcome.
interfaces.authority: Execution requires actual enabling isolation/resource/security evidence. No arbitrary YAML/code/secret/network/host access follows repository permission. Deployment requires current exact target authority/approval and valid artifact/data/recovery conditions.
interfaces.meaning: Definition/evaluated revision, run/attempt, output identity, cancellation-request versus stop, actual terminal versus unknown and target effect are different. Logs/artifacts require separate bounded access; build/merge/release is not deploy permission.
interfaces.lifecycle: Do not expose secrets through inputs/results/diagnostics or recover old authority by replay. Output retention/cleanup is scoped and reference-aware; failed work does not automatically remove required evidence or reverse target effects.
interfaces.repetition: Queue cancellation versus running stop is distinguished; completion can win cancellation race. Retry is a separately eligible new attempt after prior effect assessment; unknown target is reconciled before consequential retry/recovery.
interfaces.capacity: Suitable isolation, limits on actual resources/output/concurrency/cleanup and target readiness require actual evidence. Existing 2-vCPU/4-GB/40-GB demo/idle readings do not prove safe untrusted execution.
interfaces.compatibility: Supported workflow syntax/triggers/features, runner/isolation, output representation, target mechanism and compatibility are not chosen. No universal external CI ecosystem compatibility, marketplace actions or arbitrary remote target capability is promised.
interfaces.gates: No demonstrated suitable execution environment or approved live target is created here; conditional logical boundary only, not execution authorization.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable

interfaces.title: Operational configuration, delivery and recovery
interfaces.people: Explicitly authorized operator and selected applicable runtime/domain/TLS, notification delivery and independent backup/recovery facilities; the grouping is not one service.
interfaces.direction: Into product/operation: permitted configuration/constraints, delivery disposition and actual protected recovery sources. Out: bounded operational requests/evidence, attributable notification attempt, eligible backup material and isolated restore findings as applicable.
interfaces.authority: Configuration/evidence access, delivery credentials and recovery source/target powers are separate. A connected Gmail account is not assumed to provide identity/recovery mail. Restoration must re-evaluate current access/external effects.
interfaces.meaning: Actual effective configuration, compatibility and measured operating result are distinct from planned setup. Delivery attempt/acceptance/receipt differ. Backup artifact/completed backup/restored bytes/scoped usable recovery are distinct evidence levels.
interfaces.lifecycle: No credential/config secrets in documentation/examples; backup coverage includes whatever required data/artifacts/relationships/configuration/keys are actually defined, not assumed. Restore does not resurrect old grants or resend/deploy by default.
interfaces.repetition: Ambiguous delivery does not justify blind duplicate notification. Restore is explicitly authorized/isolated and same-candidate reconciliation precedes further effects; maintenance interruption and current environment must be identified.
interfaces.capacity: Actual backup/delivery/runtime suitability, coverage/retention and workload/recovery targets need scoped evidence. No RPO/RTO, extra infrastructure purchase, notification provider or backup schedule is invented.
interfaces.compatibility: Existing Ubuntu/Laravel demo software/resources are observations, not final technology selection or proof of current dependency health. Exact non-secret configuration/procedure/versions/TLS/delivery/recovery interfaces remain later justified design/operating work.
interfaces.gates: Backups are not configured; no usable recovery demonstrated. Notification/runtime configuration evidence is not inferred from Gmail access or a working login page; no fresh host/provider operation is performed.
interfaces.status: Proposed logical interface refinement; accepted profile core retained where applicable
